clue.text: Second group of shops retaining small quantity of coffee, say ultimate in espresso coffee

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: the shop chain holds the measure within it, so one piece is kept inside the other

parts.note: a chain is a group of shops under one owner
cc, a cubic centimetre, is a small measure of a liquid such as coffee

indicators.note: the ultimate letter in a word is its last one, here of espresso

parts.note: last letter of espresso

explanation.surface: A recipe-like instruction for a coffee chain blending a small measure with an espresso.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small quantity of coffee, say' is a cubic centimetre, the measure used for any liquid; the definition is the final 'coffee'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mochaccino is a chocolate-flavoured cappuccino, a kind of coffee drink.

clue.text: Judicial decision curtailed by depression of the elderly?

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, so the last letter of the ruling is dropped

parts.note: a decree is a ruling made by a court
a pit is a hollow or depression in the ground

explanation.surface: A court ruling that leaves old people feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrepit describes someone worn out and feeble with age, a state typical of very old people, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Animosity surrounds source of Russian icon

indicators.note: the spite word goes around the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: spite is ill will or animosity

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

parts.note: first letter of Russian

explanation.surface: Hostility gathers around a Russian religious icon.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an Orthodox religious painting, but the icon here is the computing sort.
explanation.definitionFit: In computing a sprite is a small graphic image moved about the screen, much like an on-screen icon.

clue.text: Small shake will do for window curtain

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
to wag is to shake or waggle, as a dog's tail

explanation.surface: A small shake of the fabric will be enough to hang a curtain.
explanation.definitionFit: A swag is a length of fabric draped in a curve across the top of a window, a curtain style.

clue.text: Fellow in basic accommodation possibly mined gold in ancient city on borders of Thrace

indicators.note: the reworked metal letters are placed inside the city's name

parts.note: Troy is the ancient city of Homer's Iliad

indicators.note: mined gold is gold dug out and worked over, and possibly says the letters are reordered
the borders of a word are its outer letters, first and last

parts.note: first and last letters of Thrace

explanation.surface: A man in rough lodgings may have dug gold in some old city near Thrace.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a playful description: a cave counts as very basic accommodation.
explanation.definitionFit: A troglodyte is a cave dweller, someone living in the most primitive kind of shelter.

clue.text: European leader giving European rejection about a European

indicators.note: the French refusal goes around the other letters

parts.note: non is French for no, a European way of saying no
a Pole is a native of Poland, a European

explanation.surface: One European leader snubbing another European in a diplomatic row.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'European rejection' is the French word for no, which fits a Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte was Emperor of the French, one of Europe's most famous rulers.

clue.text: Science presented in video is likely to stick

indicators.note: the science piece is shown inside the video piece, so one goes within the other

explanation.surface: A science programme shown on video will stay in viewers' minds.
explanation.definitionFit: Viscid means sticky and thick, as a glue-like liquid is.

clue.text: Women collectively behave very heartlessly

indicators.note: without their hearts, so only the outer letters of each word are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of behave
first and last letters of very

explanation.surface: Women as a group acting very cruelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Bevy is the traditional collective noun for a group of women, as with larks or quails.

clue.text: Master no longer wanting to be in charge?

parts.note: over means finished, no longer happening
power is what someone wanting to be in charge seeks; read with the first piece, over power means done with authority

explanation.surface: A boss who has grown tired of being in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a whimsical reading: someone 'over power' is past caring about authority.
explanation.definitionFit: To master something is to overcome or subdue it, the verb sense of overpower.

clue.text: I left in time, moving smartly

indicators.note: the I and L go inside the time word

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone saying they left on time, walking briskly.
explanation.definitionFit: Agile describes someone nimble and quick on their feet, able to move briskly.

clue.text: Husband getting wrong fish

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogy and listings
erring means doing wrong, straying

explanation.surface: A husband buys the wrong fish at the market.
explanation.definitionFit: The herring is a common silvery food fish of the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Bad-tempered member of comedy team finishing early before end of day

indicators.note: the name stops before its final letter

parts.note: Groucho was one of the Marx Brothers comedy team

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: last letter of day

explanation.surface: A comedian goes home early, grumpy at the end of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Grouchy means irritable and grumbling, in a sour mood.

clue.text: Met, perhaps, by rear of these trees

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police, an example of cops

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its last letter

parts.note: last letter of these

explanation.surface: Someone was met near the back of a clump of trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Met' reads as a past tense verb, but it is the Met, London's police force.
explanation.definitionFit: A copse is a small thicket or group of trees.

clue.text: Large piece of infrastructure, clean, mostly constructed from the rear

parts.note: to hoover is British for to vacuum-clean, from the Hoover brand

indicators.note: reading from the rear means the letters are read backwards
mostly means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: made means built or constructed

explanation.surface: A big project that was cleaned and largely built from the back.
explanation.walkthrough: MADE minus its last letter is MAD, and 'from the rear' turns it to DAM.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hoover Dam is a huge concrete dam on the Colorado River, a major civil engineering structure.

clue.text: Noticed his bent towards pleasure

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spotted his leaning towards a good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent towards' reads as one phrase meaning inclined to, but 'bent' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedonistic means devoted to the pursuit of pleasure, oriented to enjoyment.

clue.text: Fitting to get informed about encounter

parts.note: meet is an old word for fitting or proper
to be up with something is to be informed about it, as up with the news

explanation.surface: It is right to be well informed before a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet up with someone is to encounter or come together with them.

clue.text: Now aiding any deaths at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: These days rescuers help when people die out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in the present era, nowadays.

clue.text: Fools picked up, taken to Court, following popular response

indicators.note: the later pieces follow the popular word, coming after it

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted, so the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: nits is British slang for fools
Ct is the abbreviation for court in addresses

explanation.surface: Fools arrested and taken to court after a popular reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: An instinct is an innate, unthinking reaction to a stimulus.

clue.text: Uppity attitude adopted by a relative about running the farm

indicators.note: the reversed attitude is taken in by the relative, sitting inside

parts.note: gran, a grandmother, is a relative

indicators.note: uppity read as up-ity says the word goes upwards in this down clue, so it is reversed

parts.note: an air is a manner or attitude

explanation.surface: A haughty air picked up by a relative who talks about running a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uppity' looks like an adjective for haughty, but in a down clue it signals reading upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrarian means relating to the cultivation of land and farming.

clue.text: Respect shown by knight in honour is excellent

parts.note: the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

indicators.note: the knight letter is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: ace means excellent
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight shows respect, saying a royal honour is excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knight' is not the honour itself here: N is chess notation, K being taken by the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisance is a show of deference or respect, such as a bow.

clue.text: Go strangely green with envy ultimately

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the letters are rearranged
ultimately points to the last letter

parts.note: last letter of envy

explanation.surface: Turning oddly green with jealousy in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like the verb 'turn', but it is the noun meaning vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Go as a noun means vigour or energy, as in full of go.

clue.text: Holiday venue providing lots of entertainment after surprised response

indicators.note: the entertainment piece comes after the exclamation

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: lots of a word but not all, so its last letter goes

parts.note: fun means entertainment

explanation.surface: A holiday spot offering plenty of fun, which draws a gasp.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea, a popular tourist resort.

clue.text: Rough vehicles heading east, circling Ohio

indicators.note: the vehicles head, or go before, the compass point
the combined letters go around the state's letter

parts.note: cars are vehicles
O is an old abbreviation for the US state of Ohio
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A bumpy journey as cars drive east and loop around Ohio.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse means rough in texture, not smooth or fine.

clue.text: Sort that is stored in glasses

indicators.note: the abbreviation is kept inside the glasses word

parts.note: specs is short for spectacles, glasses
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A kind of thing kept in spectacle cases.
explanation.definitionFit: A species is a kind or type of thing, a sort.

clue.text: Sport over following result

indicators.note: the over letter follows the result word

parts.note: a sum is the result of adding
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A sporting match finished, after a result.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumo is Japanese wrestling, a sport.

clue.text: Bird: pointer given to 22A

indicators.note: the pointer is given to the species abbreviation, added after it

parts.note: 22 across is SPECIES, abbreviated sp in biology
an arrow is a pointer

explanation.surface: A bird labelled with a pointer showing its species.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparrow is a small brown songbird.

clue.text: Feeling unwell? No time for criticism

indicators.note: no time means the time letter is removed from the word

parts.note: stick is informal for harsh criticism, as in giving someone stick

explanation.surface: Someone too ill to have patience for criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: Sick means ill, physically unwell.

clue.text: Attractive, but avoiding trap? Excellent

indicators.note: avoiding the trap means the trap's letters are left out

parts.note: magnetic means attractive, drawing others in
a net is a trap

explanation.surface: Something alluring but cleverly sidestepping a snare is wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Magic is informal British for excellent or wonderful.

clue.text: An insect's fluttering without pause

indicators.note: fluttering means flapping about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An insect's wings beating nonstop.
explanation.definitionFit: Incessant means continuing without interruption or stopping.
